AirTag is a great way to protect and track your luggage, but attaching it to smaller items like cameras can be challenging.

Some people simply place an AirTag in a regular case and clip it to a camera strap, but that's not very discreet—a thief could easily spot it and toss it. Fortunately, there are better ways…

Apple has always stressed that the AirTag's main purpose isn't anti-theft. Its anti-tracking feature means a thief will eventually get notified that an AirTag is present. However, before that notification kicks in, you have several hours to track your belongings, which is why many people still use it this way.

Of course, if a thief spots and discards the AirTag quickly, that window disappears. That's why ordinary cases—while cheap and easy to install—are easily detected by thieves.

Luckily, there are more discreet ways to mount an AirTag on a DSLR or mirrorless camera.

Camera strap clips

The most basic method is a camera strap clip. These accessories look like part of the strap itself, and if you're using a black camera strap—especially a thicker comfort style—it's even less noticeable.

Quick-release plates

Many photographers keep a tripod quick-release plate permanently attached to their camera for frequent daily mounting. You can buy plates with a built-in AirTag slot, which draws less attention.

Tripod adapters

If it's hard to find a quick-release plate compatible with your tripod, another option is a universal adapter.

Cages

If you use a camera cage to mount accessories, you can either buy one with a built-in AirTag slot or add a separate slot with a cage-specific mount. The latter isn't very discreet on its own, but when installed on a fully kitted-out cage, it usually blends right in.

L-brackets

The newest accessory is Peak Design's Field Bracket. It's an L-bracket that lets you mount a camera horizontally or vertically on a tripod, with extra features like a hand strap mount and a multi-hole baseplate for expanding your rig. However, it doesn't use an AirTag—it has a built-in tracking tag compatible with Find My.

Do you use any of these methods, or have other tricks? Share them in the comments.
